mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for three consecutive months signals improving supply capacity and economic momentum, which supports higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO expansion is not followed by a statistically significant positive average 20-day S&P 500 return (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 50,000 jobs combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by at least 0.3 percentage points signals labor market weakening, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month by > 50,000 AND UNRATE > previous month by >= 0.3pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for two consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which drags on construction-related and material sector earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month MA by > 10% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 4.5% during a period of negative GDP growth (GDPC1 YoY < 0%) signals an emergency easing, which boosts risk asset valuations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% from the previous month during a period of stable consumer prices (CPIAUCSL change < 0.2% MoM) signals supply-side disruption without inflationary pressure, which reduces earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by > 2% AND abs(CPIAUCSL change) < 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, compressing margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
